messages:
Ruth (AE): Heads-up: Prospect (Greenline) asks for Private VPC POC. Hard requirements: single /30 allowlist for egress, TLS inspection by their appliance (so SNI may be stripped), and proof that client src IPs reach their app for fraud scoring. Any quick architecture notes?
Samir (Solutions): Short: three deployment choices: (1) Connector deployed in-customer VPC (best for srcIP + BYOIP), (2) PrivateLink interface endpoint to our connector (minimal route changes, ENIs in their subnets), (3) PrivateLink + customer-side passthrough TCP proxy to preserve srcIP. Tradeoffs: fixed /30 EIP from our side forces SNAT and loses srcIP unless connector is hosted inside customer account.
Priya (NetSec): TLS inspection: if they terminate TLS on their perimeter, SNI can be removed. Ask them to either: (A) allow passthrough for our hostnames, or (B) import our cert into their inspection appliance and keep SNI. If neither is possible, we must run the connector in their VPC so traffic never leaves their inspection domain before hitting app.
Hana (NetOps): For the /30 allowlist we can coordinate a support ticket to reserve two EIPs for the POC (control-plane + metrics). Warning: SNAT will rewrite client IP. If they accept a customer-hosted connector we don't need to provide EIPs.
Ruth (AE): Procurement asked for a one-paragraph network blurb to paste into their security questionnaire. Can we get a copy-paste?
Samir (Solutions): Paste below (short):

"Network Architecture (Private POC): Redwood supports deploying a customer-hosted connector inside the customer's VPC (recommended for source IP preservation and BYOIP) or using AWS Interface Endpoints (PrivateLink) to create connector ENIs in customer subnets (recommended for minimal routing changes). Connector communicates outbound to Redwood control plane over TLS (TCP/443). If customer requires a strict egress allowlist, Redwood can provide a small set of egress EIPs for allowlisting; note that centralized SNAT to our EIPs will not preserve original client source IPs unless the connector is hosted within the customer's account. For TLS inspection/SNI passthrough, we recommend allowing TLS passthrough for Redwood hostnames or registering our certs with the inspection appliance."
Hana (NetOps): Minimal SG snippet to paste into their runbook:

# Allow app to reach interface endpoint ENIs (example CIDR)
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id sg-app --protocol tcp --port 443 --cidr 10.10.20.0/24
# Allow connector to reach Redwood control plane (example small block)
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-egress --group-id sg-connector --protocol tcp --port 443 --cidr 198.51.100.8/30

Priya (NetSec): Also flag: if fraud scoring must see true client IP, confirm the logging layer: ALB/NLB can preserve X-Forwarded-For but some managed LBs replace source IP. Recommend app-level verification during POC.
Ruth (AE): Great. Procurement also wants a cost delta vs Dedicated and any onboarding fees. Samir, can you provide a short note?
Samir (Solutions): Quick pricing note: Private deploy (customer-hosted connector) = onboarding fee + platform license; POC single-AZ ~ small uplift vs hosted (~1.1-1.3x) depending on infra. If Redwood manages connector with reserved EIPs, add monthly connector infra fee. I'll supply a formal estimate in the quote.
provision-bot: POC workspace created: redwood-poc-greenline-2026 (id poc-gl-77). Link: https://internal.redwood/pocs/poc-gl-77
Ruth (AE): Thanks team. I'll send the blurb + SG snippet to Greenline and ask them to confirm whether TLS inspection can be bypassed for our hostnames or if they prefer connector-in-VPC.
